title: Mary Had a Little Lamb (arranged for beginners)
subtitle: Traditional American melody, five-finger setting in F major
trains: A very well-known three/four-note melody that never leaves a five-finger hand position, over a single sustained bass note per bar - an easy first piece for a fixed hand position.

provenance.author: Musicanyya practice material
provenance.basedOn: Sarah Josepha Hale's poem "Mary's Lamb" (Boston, 1830). The tune is the traditional one also sung as "Merrily We Roll Along"; it was checked against The child's own music book (ed. A. E. Wier, New York, 1918), p. 49, where it is printed in F major. Both are public domain.
provenance.note: 8-bar beginner form in F major (the key of the 1918 printing), so the melody sits in a single five-finger hand position (F-G-A-Bb-C), quarter=96. The left-hand single bass note per bar (I-V) is our own simple setting.

departures: Values doubled: each bar is one 2/4 bar of the familiar tune written in 4/4 (eighths become quarters).
Rhythm made plain: the dotted "Ma-ry" in bars 1 and 5 is two even notes, and the last F in bar 8 is held for the whole bar.
Left hand: our own single bass note per bar; the printing has its own piano part.
